text: Is the BRC Analytics federated service working right now, and what can't it do?

Abstract
The question asked whether the BRC Analytics federated MCP service is working now and what it cannot do. I queried the BRC Analytics MCP status endpoint using the federated check tool (brc_federation_status). The single snapshot returned version 0.29.0, health status "healthy" with timestamp 2026-09-17T21:54:44.684848, reachable: true, and a list of 5 known limitations. I counted the limitations (n = 5) directly from the returned known_limitations array and tabulated each limitation's "tool/endpoint", "problem", "use_instead", and "verified" fields as provided. These results show the MCP service is reachable and reports healthy, but five specific tool/endpoint limitations remain (search_ena_keywords, search_ena, the /ena/study/{accession} endpoint, all catalog tools re: resistance phenotypes, and the MCP endpoint URL handling). This matters because clients and downstream workflows must avoid or replace the affected tools (the response includes recommended alternatives) and must call the slashed MCP URL to avoid an HTTPS-to-HTTP downgrade error.

I. Introduction
Background. BRC Analytics provides a federated "MCP" API that aggregates and exposes multiple bioinformatics data and search tools. Users and automated clients depend on its availability and on documented limitations to route queries correctly.

Literature Review. The MCP status record was retrieved from the BRC Analytics MCP status tool call (see References for provenance). No other literature or external PubMed records were fetched for this query.

Knowledge Gap. Before querying, it was unknown whether the MCP service was reachable at this moment and which specific tool behaviors or endpoints the service itself considered limited or broken.

Objective & Hypothesis. Objective: determine current MCP reachability/health and enumerate limitations the MCP reports. Hypothesis: the MCP will report a health status and list any known limitations with recommended workarounds.

II. Materials and Methods
Study Design. Single-timepoint status check of the BRC Analytics MCP service using the dedicated federation-status tool provided by the environment. I extracted the health fields and enumerated reported limitations.

Materials. The BRC Analytics MCP status endpoint was queried via the brc_federation_status tool in this environment.

Procedures.
- Tool call 1: functions.brc_federation_status with parameters {} (no filters). This single call produced the JSON status snapshot used for all downstream reporting.

Statistical Analysis. All reported numbers are direct reads from the returned JSON. The count of known limitations equals the length of the returned known_limitations array (denominator = 1 JSON response). No deduplication was required. Fields read verbatim: version.version, health.status, health.timestamp, reachable, known_limitations (array). The number of limitations (5) is the cardinality of known_limitations.

III. Results
Table 1: MCP snapshot summary
| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| mcp_url | https://brc-analytics.org/api/v1/mcp/ |
| version | 0.29.0 |
| health.status | healthy |
| health.timestamp | 2026-09-17T21:54:44.684848 |
| reachable | true |
| number_of_known_limitations | 5 |

Table 2: Known limitations reported (one row per limitation)
| # | tool / endpoint | problem | use_instead | verified |
|---|---:|---|---|---:|
| 1 | search_ena_keywords | Sends an unquoted scientific_name to ENA; ENA answers HTTP 400. The failure is returned as tool text, so it can read like an answer. | brc_ena_search | 2026-09-17 |
| 2 | search_ena | Caps at 50 rows with has_more: true, and never reports a total. | brc_ena_runs | 2026-09-17 |
| 3 | /api/v1/ena/study/{accession} endpoint | Answers HTTP 500 for every accession tried. | brc_ena_study | 2026-09-17 |
| 4 | all catalog tools | The catalog holds no resistance phenotypes and only 2 Escherichia coli assemblies (K-12 MG1655, O157:H7 Sakai). It answers 'what can I compute, on which genome', not 'how many resistant strains are there'. | Say so plainly; route phenotype questions to BV-BRC or CARD. | 2026-09-17 |
| 5 | mcp endpoint itself | https://brc-analytics.org/api/v1/mcp without the trailing slash answers 307 to a plain http:// URL. The MCP client refuses an https-to-http downgrade, so it surfaces as an HTTP error. | Always call the slashed URL. | 2026-09-17 |

Findings. The MCP service snapshot reports reachable = true and health.status = "healthy" at the timestamp given. There are 5 known limitations listed; for each the response provides the failure description and recommended alternative or mitigation.

IV. Discussion
Interpretation. The MCP service is currently reachable and reports a healthy status in this snapshot. Despite overall reachability, five concrete limitations exist and are documented in the status response; users should avoid the affected tools or use the recommended alternatives/workarounds.

Context. The specific limitations map to ENA-search wrappers (two separate search_ena* tools and an ENA study endpoint), to limitations in the catalog (missing resistance phenotype coverage and sparse E. coli assemblies), and to a URL-handling hazard (missing trailing slash causing an https-to-http downgrade that clients reject). Each limitation entry includes a recommended alternative or mitigation and a verification date of 2026-09-17.

Limitations. The status snapshot is a single-timepoint report (timestamp provided) and may change; availability may differ after this timestamp. The MCP status is self-reported by the service; it documents known issues but may omit undiscovered failures. The status JSON does not include detailed failure logs or error rates over time. The recommended "use_instead" entries are the service's suggestions; I did not independently verify the suggested alternative endpoints or their functionality beyond this single status call.

Conclusion & Future Directions. Conclusion: the MCP service is reachable and reports healthy now, but clients must respect the five documented limitations and follow the recommended alternatives (notably use brc_ena_search or brc_ena_runs instead of the broken ENA keyword/limited-search wrappers, and always call the slashed MCP URL). A useful next query would be to programmatically test the suggested alternative endpoints (brc_ena_search, brc_ena_runs, brc_ena_study) to confirm their behavior in practice and to test the MCP endpoint without and with the trailing slash to reproduce the reported URL-handling issue.

References
[1] BRC Analytics MCP status JSON (brc_federation_status tool result). Provenance URL: https://brc-analytics.org/api/v1/mcp/

Acknowledgments
The authors of the BRC Analytics MCP status record (BRC Analytics / brc-analytics.org).
